next_steps: Sofia: share updated caching dashboard and hit-rate csv by 2026-11-27
Daniel: run 10k prompt benchmark with adjusted prefix thresholds and share results by 2026-12-01
Finly: provide representative prompt set (20-30) and traffic profile by 2026-11-30
Schedule follow-up call to review benchmark and decide on dedicated capacity - target week of 2026-12-07
action_items: Sofia - send caching dashboard link and short notes - due 2026-11-27
Daniel - rerun KV cache test (lower threshold) and post CSV - due 2026-12-01

summary: Weekly POC sync focused on prefix/KV cache hit rates and prompt reuse strategy. Finly saw overall prefix cache hit rate ~42% last week; after tuning suggestions from Redwood SE, expected to reach ~55-65% for canonical prompts. Discussed trade-offs: aggressive prefix matching improves hit-rate but can risk stale responses when prompts mutate. Action items: share dashboard, run adjusted KV benchmarks, provide prompt set and traffic sample, follow-up next week to decide on dedicated capacity pilot if hit-rate improves.
questions: What is the safe prefix length threshold before semantic mismatch increases?
How to handle prompt templating and variable slots to maximize reuse?
Do we need dedicated capacity for consistent KV cache performance?
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, will run about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Aisha here.
[00:10] Tom Rivera: Tom.
[00:11] Priya Shah: Priya.
[00:12] Ethan Gomez: Ethan.
[00:15] Daniel Park: Daniel from Redwood.
[00:17] Clara Liu: Clara.
[00:20] Sofia Martinez: Great. Quick agenda, hit rates review, tuning suggestions, then benchmark plan and next steps. Aisha, do you want to kick with the hit-rate numbers from your dashboard?
[00:33] Aisha Khan: Yeah sure, so last week we saw a prefix cache hit rate around forty two percent across our chat assistant workload, that's aggregated across low, med, high verbosity traffic. KV cache hit for completions specifically is a bit lower, about 36%. There was, uh, one anomaly on Tuesday where a deploy changed prompt ordering and hit rate dipped to 28% for a day.
[00:53] Daniel Park: Okay that aligns with what we saw in our logs; the deploy likely changed a leading context token or added a newline, small changes that can kill prefix matches. Were those templated prompts or free-form?
[01:05] Aisha Khan: Mostly templated, but the product team has started experimenting with a dynamic intro that includes user meta, so micro-variations.
[01:13] Sofia Martinez: Cool. Daniel, quick remind on how Redwoods prefix matching works in the pilot runtime? I know we have a configurable threshold but maybe best to say it here.
[01:22] Daniel Park: Yeah, so the runtime uses a contiguous prefix string match for the fast cache layer and a hash-based KV lookup for canonicalized prompts. We support fuzzy matching via normalization rules — whitespace collapse, basic punctuation strip, and optional slot masking. By default threshold is strict exact for prefix, but you can enable prefix-normalization and shorter, uh, prefix windows to increase hit rates. Trade-off is you might return a cached response that doesn't reflect a subtle variable like timestamp.
[01:46] Priya Shah: What's the recommended prefix length? We saw better results when we limited to first 120 characters but those sometimes felt off.
[01:55] Daniel Park: For templated prompts, we'd recommend canonicalizing variable slots (e.g. {{user_name}}) so the prefix captures intent rather than ephemeral tokens. If you can't canonicalize, a mid-range prefix, 80-120 chars, is reasonable. Shorter than 60 risks being too generic, longer than 200 is brittle.
[02:12] Tom Rivera: On our end we can add slot markers pretty easily, the problem is older prompts are in a few places in the codebase.
[02:19] Sofia Martinez: Noted. Aisha, do you have the distribution by prompt type? Which flows are giving most cache hits?
[02:26] Aisha Khan: Yeah the onboarding flow and FAQ responders are highest — onboarding had like 68% prefix hit last week because prompts are highly repetitive, whereas creative-writing flows basically zero hit rate.
[02:38] Daniel Park: That makes sense. So the low-hanging fruit is to target onboarding and FAQ first. If we can canonicalize 15-20 onboarding prompts we should see a bump.
[02:48] Ethan Gomez: One thing we wanted to call out — in production the cold-start of the KV cache can also be impacted by autoscaling, if the route scales to new GPU nodes the local in-memory cache needs warm-up. Do you see cross-node cache sharing?
[03:00] Daniel Park: Right now pilot runtime shares a global KV store across nodes but local L1 in-memory prefix cache is node-local for latency. On a scale-up you'll see reduced L1 hit until warm-up; we have suggestions: pre-warm with synthetic traffic, or pin high-volume routes to dedicated nodes.
[03:17] Sofia Martinez: That ties to the dedicated capacity question. If hit-rate is sensitive to scale events, dedicated pools help keep L1 warm.
[03:24] Priya Shah: What's the observed improvement when pinning routes?
[03:27] Daniel Park: In our benchmarks we saw up to 10-15% additional L1 hit improvement on steady traffic when routes are pinned vs fully autoscaled shared pools. For KV store hit it's less dramatic.
[03:39] Tom Rivera: We ran the KV bench you provided last sprint, I posted the CSV to the shared folder but I realize the threshold settings were default. What would you recommend we change?
[03:49] Daniel Park: Two knobs: prefix-normalization (enable), and canonical-slot masking for KV hashing. Also lower the minimal prefix length from 40 to 24 for the KV tier to capture shorter identical intents, but keep a length cap so you don't match on one-word prompts.
[04:05] Aisha Khan: If we lower to 24, won't we get false positives when users type short queries like "help"?
[04:11] Daniel Park: Good point. That's why we recommend combining with frequency thresholds — only apply shorter prefix matching for prompts that appear at least N times per day. For rare queries keep stricter matching.
[04:23] Sofia Martinez: Practical ops ask — can you automate that frequency threshold policy per-route?
[04:28] Daniel Park: Yes, we can turn on workload-aware thresholds; Redwood Optimize has a small rule engine to suggest per-route thresholds based on token distribution. In the pilot we can run suggestions and push a recommended config.
[04:40] Priya Shah: In terms of implementation effort, how much to canonicalize slots across the 15 onboarding prompts?
[04:46] Tom Rivera: I estimate maybe 2-3 engineer days to find and add slot markers across services, maybe 1 day for QA.
[04:52] Aisha Khan: That seems doable.
[04:55] Daniel Park: Nice. On benchmarks — we'll rerun KV tests with lower prefix length and slot masking enabled. We should see KV hit move from 36% to somewhere in the 50s for templated flows, maybe overall to mid 40s depending on traffic mix.
[05:08] Sofia Martinez: Can you put a conservative and optimistic eta in the notes?
[05:12] Daniel Park: Conservative: +2 weeks for engineering + benchmark; optimistic: +5 days if Finly provides the prompt set and we run synthetic warm-up.
[05:22] Aisha Khan: We'll try to get you the prompt set this week.
[05:25] Ethan Gomez: Quick question about freshness — some onboarding prompts include user-specific state (e.g., last login time) that we cannot cache. How do we avoid returning stale data?
[05:36] Daniel Park: Two approaches: mask those variables during cache key generation so that values don't affect the key, and add a validation token in the cached response that is re-evaluated at request time; or exclude prompts with time-sensitive slots from cache. Usually masking works if you can derive the slot's semantic equivalence.
[05:53] Priya Shah: Ok. On instrumentation, can we get per-route hit rates in the dashboard broken down by L1 vs KV?
[05:59] Sofia Martinez: Yes, dashboard supports L1/L2 breakdown. I'll send the dashboard link after the call.
[06:05] Tom Rivera: I saw the dashboard but the timestamps on events are slightly offset, looks like timezone mismatch in our logs. Not a blocker but FYI.
[06:12] Daniel Park: We'll double-check time sync and ingestion delays.
[06:16] Sofia Martinez: Alright let's move to acceptance criteria for this pilot. Aisha, what does success look like for you in two weeks?
[06:23] Aisha Khan: For us, success is a 15-20% absolute uplift in overall cache hit rate and measurable latency reduction on onboarding flows (p99 drop by at least 50-100 ms). Also we want to see stable behavior across deploys.
[06:36] Daniel Park: That's achievable if we canonicalize and tune thresholds. With dedicated pinning bump we might even see 20-25% on onboarding.
[06:44] Sofia Martinez: If we hit those numbers, we'll propose a small dedicated pilot — one or two pinned nodes for the high-volume routes. That will be a commercial discussion but it's the natural next step.
[06:55] Priya Shah: Ok makes sense. Aisha, any legal/security blockers for sharing prompt samples?
[06:59] Aisha Khan: We'll scrub PII, but yes we can share redacted prompts. Should be fine.
[07:06] Sofia Martinez: Great. Admin notes: I will post the dashboard link and a short runbook. Daniel will rerun the KV benchmark with the lowered prefix setting and slot masking enabled. Finly to post prompt set and confirm whether we can mirror 48 hours of traffic for a baseline.
[07:20] Ethan Gomez: One operational note — if we mirror traffic we need rate-limits and we're comfortable with synthetic traffic mode. We'll confirm infra constraints.
[07:28] Daniel Park: Also we can provide a small python script to canonicalize prompts if you want, low-friction.
[07:33] Tom Rivera: Yes please, that would speed things.
[07:35] Sofia Martinez: Ok we are at about 35 minutes, any final questions?
[07:40] Priya Shah: None from product.
[07:42] Aisha Khan: Nope.
[07:44] Daniel Park: Quick note on failure modes — if hit rate jumps but quality drops we'll add a fall-through policy to prefer fresh model calls for certain safety-sensitive routes.
[07:54] Sofia Martinez: Good, put that in the runbook. Last recap of next steps: share dashboard, rerun benchmarks, provide prompt set, discuss pinning dedicated nodes if numbers look good. We'll reconvene next week same time. Thanks everyone.
[08:12] Tom Rivera: Thanks all.
[08:14] Priya Shah: Bye.
[08:15] Sofia Martinez: Bye.
